main_text.p: annum vigesimū nonū ætatis, quod repugnat histo-cc riæ Euangelicæ. Porrò Christum passum esse circacc tempus vernum currente anno decimo octauo im-cc perii Tiberii, euidenter probat Eusebius Cæsari-cc ensis ab admiranda illa circa passionem Dominicamcc eclipsi solis, quæ in commentariis Ethnicorum dili-cc genter fuit consignata. is ait, Secundùm prophetiascc quæ de Deo fuerant prælocutæ, ad passionem ve-cc nit anno Tiberii XVIII. quo tempore & in aliis Ethni-cc corum commentariis hæc ad verbum scripta repe-cc rimus. Solis facta defectio, & tenebræ super vni-cc uersam terram. Bithynia terræ motu concussa, &cc in vrbe Nicæna ædes plurimæ corruerunt: quæ o-cc mnia his congruunt, quæ in passione Saluatoris ac-cc ciderunt. Scripsit verò super his & Phlegon, quicc Olympiadum egregius supputator est, in decimocc quarto libro ita dicens: Quarto autem anno du-cc centesimæ secundæ Olympiadis, magna & excel-cc lens inter omnes, quæ ante eam acciderant, defe-cc ctio solis est facta. dies hora sexta ita in tenebro-cc sam noctem versus, vt stellæ cœlo visæ sint, ter-cc ræque motus in Bithynia Nicænæ vrbis multas æ-cc des subuerterit. Hæc supra dictus vir. Argumentumcc autem huius rei, quòd Saluator isto anno passus sit,cc Euangelium præbet Ioannis, in quo scribitur, postcc quintum decimum annum Tiberii Cæsaris tribuscc annis Dominum prædicasse. Annus quartus Olym-cc piadis ducentesimæ secundæ, hoc est, annus Olym-cc piadicus octingentesimus octauus, cœpit à solsti-cc tio, labente anno Iuliano feptuagefimo feptimo:cc itaque passio Dominica subsequente vere incurrit incc annum Iulianum feptuagefimum octauum, hoc eft,

page.notes: The right-margin signs are printed as small "cc"-like marks, one beside nearly every line. I could not read them with certainty and have transcribed them only approximately as "cc"; they may be ditto or section marks. The line-end positions of the marks are also approximate. The word "octingentesimus" and the line "piadicus octingentesimus octauus" are as printed, though the sense is unclear; "feptuagefimo" and "feptuagefimum" were read as printed, with long s written as s. The page number at the top right reads 399 but the third digit is slightly unusual in the scan. The text ends mid-sentence, so the paragraph continues on the next page. No catchword or signature is visible.
